build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

left by earlier loads after the load stub; the Jam does not write or read them

comments.text: The CPU port's data direction register ($00); the Jam leaves it as the loader set it.
The CPU port: $25 while the Jam runs (BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out, I/O in), $24 (all RAM) inside unpack_shape and move_shape_file; raster_irq saves and restores it.

Load stub copied here by the resident event manager (run_load_stub $FA58, template $F925, row 4 of its load table): loads file $28, the Downhill Jam's main program, to $0880 with load_file $F230, masks interrupts, sets CIA 1 port A to output and port B to input, selects keyboard row 7 ($DC00 = $7F) and jumps to $0880. The file number at $0801 is the only byte that differs from High Jump's copy of this stub.

Program entry. On the first run $0880 is JSR jam_load_files ($2140), which loads files $29-$30 and then overwrites $0880-$0882 with three NOPs, so PRACTICE AGAIN (the stub's JMP $0880, re-run without loading) falls straight through to jam_init ($1FEA). Then: copy $FE0F (slot B is LESTER) to $3D79, clear the two control choices $3D94/$3D95 unless $FE11 says practice (so a practice rerun keeps GOOFY/REGULAR), and fall into the main loop.
Operand of the JSR at $0880 (jam_load_files, $2140); $216C-$2174 overwrite it and the opcode with $EA, so in the play snapshot $0880-$0882 read NOP NOP NOP.
High byte of the JSR operand at $0880, turned into a NOP by $2174 after the first load.

Main loop, one pass per frame or more. For each player whose frame flag $3C96 (set to 2 by the frame interrupt, $231C) is up it runs player_animation_tick ($1052) and then player_update ($16BE, which decrements $3C96), then toggles the current player $3D0F, runs both players' sideways-movement steps ($2A31, $29E7), the player-against-player fight check ($0BCF), the animated characters ($0BA6), the end-of-race check ($15B0), the bump check ($0DD6), the start check ($14F0), the status texts ($095F, $0991), the score counter ($0A28), the finish texts ($09DA) and the keyboard ($1532), and loops. $28/$29/$3C7D/$3C7E/$3CB6 are reset to defaults on every pass.

Called once per frame from the band-1 interrupt ($2398): hands the pending sound request $3D86 to the sound driver's queue (queue_sound_id $E03E) and clears it and $3D87/$3D8D to $FF. While the sound flag copy $3D93 is 0 (music wanted and not yet started) it first makes the request sound $15 (21, the music) and sets $3D93 = $FF, so the music is requested once after start-up or after the Commodore key turns it back on.

Request sound ID A for this frame (delivered by deliver_pending_sound, $0917): store it in $3D8D and make it the pending request $3D86 if nothing is pending ($FF) or its priority in sound_priorities ($E778) is at least that of the pending one. Only one sound per frame survives, the highest priority; Y is preserved. Called with A = $FF by jam_init to clear the request.
Auto symbol from the RESET vector at $FFFC ($0954, left by earlier programs): the BCC inside request_sound. Part of request_sound.

Status line: once per player (flag $3D56,x), print the player's name (pointer $35FA/$35FC,x, from $FE00/$FE09) at row $3600,x, column $35FE,x in colour $3602,x, unless the player is still in state 9 (waiting at PRESS YOUR BUTTON).

Status line: once per player after its button press ($3D3F,x set, $3D58,x not yet), print at row+1 the player's score label: column +$0F, the score digits $3C90/$3C92 with print_bcd ($2262) after a separator ($09D5). Clears the separator flags $3C7D/$3C7E around the digits so leading zeros are suppressed.
Print screen code $3A (':') at the text cursor through print_char ($2210); used between the score's digit groups.
Once per player after its button press (flag $3D5A,x): print SCORE: ($35B9) at row+1 of the player's status block and the three BCD score bytes $3C90/$3C92/$3C94 after it, in colour $0F.

Runs every main-loop pass for the current player $3D0F. Every 16 passes it flips the blink phase $3D4D. When points are pending in $3C43,x (BCD, with $3C47,x the low digits) it adds them to the score $3C90-$3C94 in decimal mode, clears $3D5A,x so the SCORE line is reprinted, moves the amount to the popup $3C45,x and starts the popup timer $3C41,x = $B0. While $3C45,x is non-zero it prints '*' + amount + '*' at column +$0E of the row below in the blink colour $3606; when the timer $3C41,x (counted down by player_update) reaches 0 it blanks the field ($35CB) and clears the amount.
Auto symbol from the NMI vector at $FFFA, which points here, into score_counter's STA $3D4D: an NMI (RESTORE) would land in the middle of this routine. Part of score_counter.

Add A (BCD) to player X's pending points $3C43,x in decimal mode. If the player's time bonus $3D74/$3D76,x has run out (both zero) the pending points are thrown away instead, so nothing scores once the bonus clock is empty.
add_points for the other player (X EOR 1), X restored: used when player X is knocked down, so the attacker gets the points (5 for a hit, $0C88, $0CC0, $0CFB, $0D1F, $0D43, $0E8B).

Step the moving object drawn into the course map in two places, rows 49-52 from column 26 ($89C2) and rows 73-76 from column 30 ($8D86), once for each count in $3CFA (added every 32 frames by the interrupt, $2331). Moving right (direction $3CF9 = 1): blank column $3CF8 in all four rows and put character $52 in the top row four columns on; moving left: draw $52, $53, $55, $54 down the column left of $3CF8 and blank the top row four columns on. $3CF8 runs 0-3; at either end the direction flips instead of a step. Only while the camera is in the top part of the course ($27 < 3) and no screen copy is running or due ($3C82, $3D15, $3D8E); each step requests a redraw ($3D14 = 1, $44 = 1, $3D0D = 0).

When the interrupt has counted another 8 frames ($74, $2329), swap the 24 bytes of characters $40-$42 with $80-$82 ($4A00/$4C00) and $60-$62 with $A0-$A2 ($4B00/$4D00) in the playfield character set: a two-frame animation of six characters.

Player-against-player attacks, once per pass, only when the skaters are within 16 pixels of each other across ($61/$62) and down the screen ($63/$64). If both face the same way (flags $3C78/$3C79) only the one behind can hit: its attack in the hitting frame ($3CF4/$3CF5), if the victim has no recovery time ($3D54/$3D55) and hit_blocked ($0D98) lets it through, knocks the one in front down (knock_down_player1 $0C6F, after the checks at $0C5C; knock_down_player0 $0C94, which makes the checks itself). Facing each other, one attack only shoves the other aside (shove_player $0D5E, 2 points) and two attacks at once go to resolve_double_attack ($0CCC). Facing apart, nothing happens.

Player 0 hits player 1 from behind: unless player 1 is already down or finished (state 4 or 6), give it a fall: recovery timer $3D54,x = $C8 (200 frames), fall animation $12, 5 points to the attacker (add_points_to_other), sound $0F, start_fall ($0F3A).

Player 1 hits player 0 from behind (when player 0 has no recovery time and hit_blocked passes it): the same fall as knock_down_player1 but for player 0 (fall $12, 200 frames, 5 points to player 1, sound $0F).

Both players are in an attack's hitting frame at once: index hit_outcome_table ($3BC9) with $3BAF[attack 1] + $3BBC[attack 0]. 0: both shoved aside (shove_both $0D53); 1: only player 0 falls ($0D2F); 2: only player 1 falls ($0D0B); 3: both fall ($0CE7). A fall is animation $11 with 200 frames of protection, 5 points to the other player and sound $0F.
Neither attack wins: push both players one step apart sideways (shove_player $0D5E for 0 and 1).

Push player X one pixel sideways, once per contact (latch $6F,x, cleared by the animation code at $1415 when the other player's attack frame ends): left if facing flag $3C78,x is set (not past column 0), right otherwise (not past $98). Gives the other player 2 points and plays sound $0E. Skipped while the player is down or finished (state 4 or 6).

Can player Y avoid player X's attack? Returns Z set (blocked) or A = 1 (lands). If Y is ducking ($3C6B,y), attacks 3, 6, 9 and $0C miss (high attacks); if Y is in the air (state 1), attacks 1, 4, 7 and $0A miss (low attacks). Anything else lands.

Body contact without attacks. Skipped while either player has recovery time ($3D54/$3D55), is down (state 4) or the contact latch $6B is set. The kind of contact comes from collision_check ($24C9) in $6A: 1 head-on, 2 side by side, 3 one behind the other, 4 crossing paths. Each sets a 30-frame bump timer $3D54,x and goes to its handler; X is not set here, so the timer goes to whichever player the routines before it left in X (in the simulator also X = $FF, after animate_charset's loop, putting the timer at $3E53 among the file's unused bytes): 1 decides who falls by speed and height ($0E26), 2 swaps speeds and headings (swap_momentum $0EE9), 3 swaps and latches ($0EE1), 4 both fall ($0EBE).

Contact kind 1: if both players are in the air (height $3C9B != ground $3C97), or both are ducking, both fall. Otherwise each gets a score of $38D8[heading/4 & 7] + its screen row ($63/$64); equal scores, both fall. The higher scorer is X, the other Y: if Y is on the ground and not ducking Y falls and X gets 5 points; if Y is in the air or ducking, X falls instead (no points). Falls use animation $0D and sound $0F.
Knock both players down: fall animation $0D, sound $0F, start_fall for player 0 and player 1; then latch $6B so the contact is handled once.
Contact from behind: swap_momentum, then latch $6B.

Players brush each other: sound $0B, swap their speeds $3D1B/$3D1C, their sideways speeds $3D1F/$3D20 and their headings $3C63/$3C64; if they face opposite ways, flip both headings by $20 (half a turn) so each keeps its own facing; then latch $6B.
Put player X into the fall state 4 with the fall animation $3D41,x (copied to $3CE4,x): speed $3D1B, the animation timers $3CE8/$3CF0 cleared.
State 4 (down) handler for every input: wait for the fall animation $3CE4,x to finish, then reset_after_fall ($0F60) and return to state 0.

Clear player X's movement after a fall or a respawn: speed, heading, lean, spin, facing, duck, jump counters, $75; then place it back on the course: column from the course's lane table at $3C0E (pairs of row, column) for its row ((y/8)+12), the left or right lane edge chosen so that it is not within 5 columns of the other player; if it ends up left of the other player it faces right ($3C63 = $20, $3C78 = 1).

Each frame from the band-0 interrupt: give the player ahead down the course ($3CF6, set by camera_follow) the lower sprite numbers 2-4 (drawn in front) and the other 5-7: $3D03/$3D04 are each player's first sprite pair, $3D08/$3D09 its third sprite. Then copy the players' colours into the sprite colour shadow $3CD0: the two body sprites get $38C5/$38C9 and the board sprite the skater's attribute $38C7/$38C8 (from $FE02/$FE0B).
Per player, per frame: toggle the double-buffer phase $3CB2 (on player 0's call), and unless the player's animation is frozen ($3D8F,x, set at the finish) run player_pose ($1068).

Choose player X's pose frames and place its three sprites. Falls and animations ($3CE4,x) run animate_sequence ($139F) with the pose bank $D940 (riding) or $DC40 (standing, falling); states 9 and 5 use the standing bank. While riding, the frame is computed from heading + spin ($3C63 + $3C5F), lean $3C5B and duck $3CFF: three part frames $3D5E (body), $3D60 (legs), $3D5C (board) and offsets $45/$47. Then build_sprite_shapes ($121D) and work out the X positions, the X high bits ($3D10, $D010 shadow) and the Y positions $3D29-$3D34 from the pose offsets, the column $61,x, the screen row $63,x and the height above ground ($3C9B - $3C97).

Build player X's three sprite shapes for the next frame: for body, legs and board, point $16 at the pose record base $3D43/$3D45 + frame * 6, set the destination block from $38B7/$38BB/$38BF + the buffer phase $3CB2 and unpack it with unpack_shape ($135C); keep each part's X/Y offsets in $3D68-$3D72. Sprite pointers $3D35/$3D37/$3D39 = $38E5-$38E9 + phase; all three sprites are set multicolour.

Copy one trimmed sprite shape into a 64-byte sprite block. ($16) points at a six-byte pose record in file $2C under the I/O area: a word offset added to $BA1A (the shape's start), the byte count minus one, an X offset and a Y offset (to $3C55/$3C56). With the CPU port at $24 (all RAM) it copies the bytes into the block whose address was patched into $138B/$1394 and zero-fills the rest of the 64 bytes.
Low byte of the shape source address in the LDA at $1387, patched by $136A ($1A + record offset).
High byte of the shape source address, patched by $1372 ($BA + record offset): shapes start at $BA1A.
Low byte of the destination sprite block in the STA at $138A, patched by build_sprite_shapes ($1259, $12AC, $12FF).
High byte of the destination block for the STA at $138A (patched with $138B).
Low byte of the destination block in the zero-filling STA at $1393, patched together with $138B.
High byte of the zero-fill destination, patched together with $138C.

Run player X's current animation $3CE4,x (1-$16: twelve attacks, the falls $0D-$12 and $15/$16, the start $13/$14). On the first call it loads from the animation tables: frame delay $3930, X offset $3919, first frame $38EB, length $3902, hitting frame $3947. Every delay+1 frames it steps to the next frame; at the end it clears the animation and returns the player to state 0 (unless down, waiting or at the start). While the step counter equals the hitting frame, $3CF4,x holds the attack number (what fight_check and smash_objects test); otherwise it is 0 and the other player's shove latch $6F is cleared. The frame indexes the part tables $395D (body), $3A23 (legs) and $3AE9 (board).

State 5 (the CONTROL: REGULAR/GOOFY choice) with a direction held: count $3D47,x up. The no-input handler ($1453) holds it at 10, so the first frame of a press reaches 11 and flips the control choice $3D94,x between REGULAR and GOOFY; holding the stick flips it again each time the byte wraps round to 11 (every 256 frames). Then show_control_choice.

State 5 with nothing pressed: set $3D47,x = 10, arming the next press to flip the control choice. For player 1 when it is LESTER ($3D79) and not yet ready, press its button for it (state5_fire_handler).

Until player X has pressed its button, print CONTROL: ($358E) and REGULAR or GOOFY ($35F6/$35F8 by $3D94,x) on its status row, set its start height ($3C9B = $23 + $42,x) and, once, pick one of the two start animations $13/$14 at random (1 in 4 for $14).
State 5 with the button: player X is ready. Set its start height, clear the animation, overwrite the CONTROL line with spaces ($35C0) and set $3D3F,x.
When both players are in state 5 and both have pressed their buttons ($3D3F/$3D40), start the race: speed 1, vertical speed $FD (a hop) and state 1 for both, and start the race clocks ($3C53/$3C54).

Read keyboard row 7 ($DC00 = $7F, $DC01 bits 7 and 5). On a change: RUN/STOP sets the quit flag $FE12, silences the sound and leaves through JMP $FE06 (event_done); the Commodore key flips the sound flag $FE10 and copies it to $3D91/$3D93, which turns the music off (the interrupt silences the driver) or back on (deliver_pending_sound requests it again). Sound effects are still requested either way.
State 6 (finished) with the button: freeze player X's animation ($3D8F,x = 1), then as state6_handler.

State 6 (past the finish): stop the player (speed, animation, lean, spin, height, clock flag) and, if any time bonus is left in $3D74/$3D76, move it into the pending points $3C47/$3C43 (score_counter adds it to the score) and clear it. LESTER (player 1 with $3D79) freezes at once.
When both players are in state 6 and both point popups and pending points are empty: hide the frozen players' sprites, and once both are frozen ($3D8F/$3D90) end the event (end_event $15F8).

Hide both players, restore the knocked-over objects in the course map (restore_course_objects $1651), reset the ground heights and joystick map, reset both players ($1687), and hand the scores to the event manager: player 0's three BCD score bytes $3C94/$3C92/$3C90 to $FE03-$FE05, player 1's $3C95/$3C93/$3C91 to $FE0C-$FE0E; silence the sound and JMP $FE06.

Repair the course map $8200-$A9FF for the next run: every knocked-over character $67, $6A, $6B, $6E, $DA, $90 is turned back into its upright form $66, $68, $69, $6D, $6F, $8F (tables $167B/$1681). Called by end_event, so PRACTICE AGAIN finds every bin and can standing.
Six characters of knocked-over objects ($67, $6A, $6B, $6E, $DA, $90), searched by restore_course_objects.
Their upright forms, in the same order ($66, $68, $69, $6D, $6F, $8F), written back by restore_course_objects.
Reset player X for a new run: clear the pose ($3017), facing, turn count, speed, heading, lean, spin, height; set the ground and terrain variables to the baseline $42,x; state 0.

One player's game step, run by the main loop for player $3D12 once per frame: steering ($1874), the map under the skater ($1F74), the terrain behaviours ($1932), smashing objects with an attack ($1702), the joystick and state handler ($2DC7) and the speed split ($1E09); then count down both players' recovery timers $3D54/$3D55 (not while down) and both score popups $3C41/$3C42.

While player X is in an attack's hitting frame ($3CF4,x) and no screen copy is running ($3D8E): scan a block of 6 columns by 3 rows of the attribute map around the skater (rows from (y + $54)/8, columns x/4 - 3 to x/4 + 2) for terrain types 6 and 4 (high nibble). Type 6 cells (bottles, cans, the hydrant) are hit by the low attacks: 1 or 7 in the left three columns, 4 or $0A in the right two, either pair in the fourth. Type 4 cells (cans and bins) are hit the same way by the straight attacks 2/8 and 5/$0B. The first hit goes to smash_object_cell ($17AA): one object per frame.

Knock over the object at ($12),y in the course map and score it: $66 can -> $67, 2 points, sound 1; $6D bottle -> $6E, 1 point, sound 0; the two-character bins $68+$69 or $69 with $68 to its left -> $6A $6B, 3 points, sound $16; $6F top of a hydrant-like object -> $DA with $90 below it, 7 points, sound $10 ($8F, its lower half, is handled from the cell above). Starts the score sparkle at the object (score_popup_small $18D4 or score_popup_large $18F8), waits for any screen copy to finish ($3C82) and asks for a redraw ($3D14, $44, $3D0D).

State 0 only: turn player X by its spin $3C5F (turn rate) one heading step per 8 units of spin, through turn_one_step ($1D41) with lean $3C5B forced to the spin's sign, slowing it down a little for each step ($306C) and easing the spin towards 0 when the heading changed.

Start the score sparkle over a smashed small object: 3 frames ($3D7B), 4 ticks each ($3D7C), at map row $3D7D / column $3D7E converted from the player's saved map position $3D7F/$3D81,x (column mod 40).
As score_popup_small but 12 frames long ($3D7B = $0C), for the bins worth 3 points.
Pseudo-random byte: shift-and-subtract step on $3C6E with $3C6F rotated in; returns $3C6E EOR $3C6F. The same generator as the music's ($AB11).

Apply the terrain under player X (not in state 8): first the sprite priority (set_ground_priority $196A), then dispatch the centre cell's type $3CA7,x through behaviour_table ($3873) by patching the JSR at $1951, and the right-hand cell's type $3CA9,x through behaviour_table_right ($3893, all sixteen entries $1969, an RTS) at $1966.
Low byte of the JSR operand at $1951, patched from behaviour_table ($3873) by the terrain type.
High byte of the patched JSR operand at $1951.
Low byte of the JSR operand at $1966, patched from behaviour_table_right ($3893); every entry there is $1969, an RTS.
High byte of the patched JSR at $1966.

Put player X's three sprites behind the background ($3CE2, the $D01B shadow) while the character under it ($3CA1,x) is $2B-$2F or $F7-$FA, the edges of tall scenery; in front otherwise. Not while down (state 4).
Terrain types 2 and 4: hit a solid object. In the air over it (shadow mode 1, $3CB4) the fall is animation $11 with sound $11, otherwise $10 with sound $0D (crash_common $1A5B).
Terrain type 3: on characters $8D/$8E fall $10 with sound $0C, otherwise fall $0E with sound 4.
Terrain type 7: fall $10 with sound 4.

Terrain type 1, walls and buildings: characters $2B, $2C, $2F give fall $15 with sound $13; $52 (the moving object) fall $10 with sound 6; any other wall character bounces the skater off: fall $16 with sound $0A (not when already down), back to ground height, and patches the fall animation's frame delay ($3946, entry $16 of anim_delay) to 11 - (speed - sideways speed).
End of the crash behaviours: clear the shadow mode; once per contact (latch $71,x) request the chosen sound $3D87, then start_fall.
Terrain type 10: raised ground. The ground height $3C97 becomes the baseline $42 + 7 and the skater is lifted to it if lower.
Terrain type 12, the lanes of the moving object (rows 50-76): unless already down or on a blank character $20 (where the object is not), fall $10 with sound 6.

Terrain type 15. Above y $0700 (rows 0-3, 53-73, 137-156): on the ground ($3C9B = $3C97) the skater slows down, one step every other frame, every frame at speed 4 or more and once more every fifth frame ($306C); on a character $60 or higher it also sets $3C70 once (sound 5), which makes the joystick read as centred at speed 2 or more ($2DE7) until the skater leaves the terrain. From y $0700 (rows 248-252, the police car): with a height under 8 the skater crashes into it (fall $10, sound $0C); with 8 or more it lands on top: height and ground 8, vertical speed 1, 8 pixels further down, $0D added to the pending points (13 in decimal mode), sound 9 made pending, state 0; once only ($3D8A,x).

Terrain type 9, the striped ramps (characters $C0-$C7, rows 121-221): on the ground and on odd y only (latch $3C3F,x), characters $C2-$C5 raise the ground $3C97 and the height by 2; other type-9 characters lower the ground by up to 2 back towards the baseline $42,x.

Terrain type 11. With the camera row $1C at $E0 or more (rows 253-254, the very bottom) this is the end of the course: state 6 ($1C81). Elsewhere (the two lines across the yard at rows 57-67): when the low byte of the skater's y is $77 or $B6, a skater who is not ducking falls ($11, sound $11); otherwise shadow mode 1 ($3CB4): the shadow sprite X ($3CB8) = column * 2, clamped to 32-$E0 with the X high bit, block $5C, X-expanded, colour $0C. Only the low byte of y is compared.
Terrain type 13 (rows 157-171, columns 0-6): shadow mode 2 ($3CB4): the shadow sprite (block $5D, colour $0C) X- and Y-expanded and behind the background, at X = column * 2 up to $28.
Player X reaches the end: state 6.

Terrain type 6: rolling over a can ($66, 2 points, sound 1) or a bottle ($6D, 1 point, sound 0) knocks it over in the map ($67/$6E), starts the sparkle for a can, asks for a redraw and costs one step of speed.

Terrain type 8, on the ground and once per contact ($40,x): character $AB (a bump) turns the skater by a random -4..+3 heading steps and costs one step of speed; $97 throws it down (fall $0F, sound 3).
Terrain types 0, 5 and 14: clear the per-terrain latches ($3C70, $3CB4, $40, $71) and set the ground back to the baseline $42,x.
Shared tail of behaviour_none and behaviour_slope: clear the shadow mode, the ground back to $42,x, the hazard and crash latches.

Add the lean $3C5B,x to the heading accumulator $3D21,x and turn one heading step per 2 units: heading $3C63 + 1 (wrapping $20 to $E0) or - 1 (wrapping $E0 to $20), with check_turnaround_right/left ($1DA1/$1DD5) and the spin update $2E46 after each step; finally $3C65 = |heading|.

After a right turn step: at heading $11 when riding forwards, or $F0 when riding backwards, the turn costs two steps of speed and, if the skater has stopped, turns it round (facing $3C78 flipped, turn count $3C8C + 1); with speed left the heading is held back one step.
The left-hand counterpart of check_turnaround_right, at headings $EF and $10.

After steering: from |heading| look up the sideways share in sideways_share ($3618: 0-15 for |heading| 0-$0F, $0A at $10, -15 to -1 for $11-$1F, 0 at $20) (signed in $3C67, magnitude $3C69), multiply it by the speed $3D1B (repeated addition with the remainder kept in $3C76) and divide by 16: sideways speed $3D25 and its signed form $3D1F. The rest of the speed goes downhill (move_player $259A).

Called for both players from the band-0 interrupt. Skipped in states 2, 3, 5, 9. In state 1 or whenever the skater is above its ground ($3C9B > $3C97 + 9 in state 1), move the height by the vertical speed $3C9D (sub-steps of 16 in $3C9F), the speed growing by 1 per step (gravity); at or below the ground: land (height = ground, vertical speed 1), and coming down from state 1 go to state 3 (the landing crouch) with sound $14.

Turn the row number in $16/$17 into pointers: $12/$13 = $8200 + row*40 (the char map) and $14/$15 = $5A00 + row*40 (the attribute map). Row times 40 is (row*4 + $35)*8, so $35 must hold the row as well.

Read the three map cells under player X's feet (row (y + $64)/8, columns x/4 - 1 to x/4 + 1): the characters to $3CA5/$3CA1/$3CA3 and their terrain types (attribute high nibble) to $3CAB/$3CA7/$3CA9; keeps the row and column in $3D7F/$3D81,x for the sparkle.
Point $12/$14 at the map row under player X (row (y + $64)/8, kept in $35 and $3C6D) and return Y = column x/4.
Fill the first three text rows of the screen at $5000 ($5000-$5077) with spaces.

Per-run set-up (every start and every PRACTICE AGAIN): save the VIC registers ($21D1), clear zero page $13-$FF and the variables $3C41-$3D93, no sound pending, fill the screen at $5000 with spaces, give each player its sprites (player 0: 5, 6 and 7; player 1: 2, 3 and 4), place both skaters ($2131), clear the status rows, select VIC bank 1 ($DD00 bits = %10) and $D018 = $42, request both screen copies ($3D14, $3D15, $44), sprite multicolours 8 and 0, black border, both players to state 9 (PRESS YOUR BUTTON), blank the screen, install the raster interrupt ($21E4), CPU port $25, IRQ vector $22A2, copy the bit masks $3608 to $4B-$5A, reset the ground baselines ($212A) and the names ($20F2), reset the sound driver ($E000), set both time bonuses to 9996 (BCD $99 $96 in $3D76/$3D74), remember the keyboard state ($3D92) and the sound flag $FE10 in $3D93/$3D91.
Copy the event manager's slot data: the board colours $FE02/$FE0B to $38C7/$38C8 and the name pointers $FE00/$FE01 and $FE09/$FE0A to $35FA-$35FD.

No joystick bytes read yet ($3D4E/$3D4F = $FF) and the default port map: player 0 reads $DC00 (port 2), player 1 $DC01 (port 1). state9_handler changes the map so that whoever presses first is player 0.
Both players' ground baselines $42/$43 = $18 (24).
Starting places: player 0 at column $2B ($61), player 1 at $78 ($62), both on screen row $48 ($63/$64).

Load the Downhill Jam's other files with the resident loader load_file ($F230), the CPU port at $25, from load_table ($353B: file numbers $29-$30, load address low bytes all 0, high bytes $82, $5A, $48, $AA, $40, $E0, $57, $AA). After the fourth file ($2C, loaded at $AA00) move_shape_file ($2189) shifts it up to $BA1A, out of the way of file $30, which loads at $AA00 next. Then write $EA over $0880-$0882 (the JSR to this routine) and set both control choices to REGULAR.
Unused: LDA #1, LDX #8, LDY #0, JMP $FFBA, the KERNAL's SETLFS for file 1 on device 8. Nothing calls it; the KERNAL is banked out while the Jam runs ($01 = $25), so it could not work here.

Copy $26 (38) pages down from the top with the CPU port at $24 (all RAM): source $A9E5-$CFE4, destination $B9FF-$DFFE, so file $2C (loaded at $AA00-$CFE5) ends up at $BA1A-$DFFE, under the I/O area. The copy stops one byte short: the file's last byte ($CFE5, which should land on $DFFF) is not moved, and the first $1B destination bytes $B9FF-$BA19 receive the bytes below the file at $A9E5-$A9FF.
Fill the screen at $5000-$53FF with spaces ($20).
Keep $D018, $DD00 and $D021 in $3C3C/$3C3E/$3C3D. Nothing in the Jam reads them back.
Disable the CIA 1 interrupts, wait for a new raster line ($2205), set the raster compare to $FB (bit 8 clear) and enable the raster interrupt.
Wait until $D012 changes and then until it is below 128 (the BMI loop): a short wait into the visible part of a frame.
Write screen code A at text row $29, column $28 of the screen at $5000 (row start from $3831/$384A) and colour $3CB6 at the same place in colour RAM, then advance the column. Y preserved.
Print the zero-terminated string at ($12) with print_char, turning ASCII capitals $41-$5A into screen codes $01-$1A; other bytes are printed as they are. Y preserved.

Print the BCD byte A as two digits through $3863 (the digit table) with print_char. Leading zeros are dropped while $3C7E is 0 (the first non-zero digit, or a forced one, sets it); $3C7D = 0 suppresses the first digit of the byte when it is 0. A preserved, Y preserved.
The RTS of print_bcd, also the handler that the null joystick row ($3821) gives states 0-7: an impossible joystick combination does nothing in those states.

The raster interrupt: save the registers and the CPU port, set $01 = $25, acknowledge, and run the handler for band $2F from band_handlers ($355B) by patching the JSR at $22D3; before calling it, move to the next band ($3567) and set its raster line ($3563), then CLI so the next band can interrupt this one. Four bands: 0 at line $F6 ($22DF, the game's frame work), 1 at $45 ($233D), 2 at $4D ($23A9), 3 at $64 ($23D3).
Low byte of the band handler JSR at $22D3, patched from band_handlers ($355B) on every interrupt.
High byte of the band handler JSR at $22D3, patched with $22D4.

Band 0, raster line $F6 (below the playfield): switch to the status line's mode for the next frame (hires text, 24 rows, $D018 = $40: screen $5000 with the font at $4000, background black, $D022/$D023 white), then the frame's work: collision_check ($24C9), the shadow sprites ($2BE9), the score sparkle ($2C12), the sprite registers ($2A96), the sprite order ($1004), the moving object ($0AF7) and the clocks ($23F8); set the frame flag $3C96 = 2 for the main loop, count frames in $73 (and $74 every 8, $3CFA every 32) and run apply_gravity for both players.

Band 1, raster line $45: nine NOPs of delay, then multicolour on, ECM on with the fine scroll $1A (24 rows) and $D018 = $12 or $42 by the displayed buffer $3D0C (screen $4400 or $5000, characters at $4800). Multicolour and ECM together are an invalid mode that shows black, which blanks the lines until band 2. Then move both players down the course ($258A), the drop-in at the bottom ($2D67), and run the sound: the driver's per-frame update ($E075) once per frame counted in $3D89 (catching up missed frames, guarded by $3D88), silencing the driver first when the Commodore key turned the music off ($3D91), and deliver_pending_sound.

Band 2, raster line $4D: wait a few cycles ($3553 by the fine scroll), then the playfield colours: background $0B, multicolour 1 $0C, multicolour 2 $00; ECM off and 40 columns, ending the black blanking lines.

Band 3, raster line $64: unless a copy is already running ($3C82), do the requested screen copies: the colour copy and buffer flip ($2742) when the camera row changed ($3D15), the character copy ($25FF) when one is due ($3D14); $3D8E says a copy ran in this frame.

Each frame, for each player whose clock runs ($3C53,x): count frames in $3C4B; every 6 frames take 6 from the time bonus $3D74/$3D76 (BCD, not below 0) and add a tenth to the race clock: tenths $3C4D, seconds $3C4F (BCD), minutes $3C51, stopping at 9:59.9. A pending penalty ($3D52,x) is applied first (add_penalty $2476).

Penalty for being left behind (set by camera_follow): add 5 seconds to the player's race clock (not past 9:55) and take 300 points (BCD $03 from the high byte) off its time bonus, or empty it. Clears $3D52,x.

Classify the contact between the two skaters for bump_check: their reach depends on heading ($38CB across, $38D8 down the screen, by heading/4). If they are further apart than the sum of reaches, or their heights differ by 5 or more, nothing ($6A = 0, $6B cleared). Otherwise $6A: 1 when their headings differ by 11-$14 (opposed), 4 when they differ by 8 or more with opposite signs (crossing), 2 when within 7 pixels down the screen (side by side), else 3. The first contact also locks both joysticks for 30 frames ($6C).
For player 1 then 0, move_player ($259A); then camera_scroll ($2891).

Move player X: the downhill part of its speed, $3D1B - $3D25 (sideways part), is added to $3D17 and every 8 units moves it a pixel down the course (inc_player_y $2872). The sideways speed $3D1F accumulates in $3D19; every 11 units one column step is flagged, right in $3CFD,x or left in $3CFB,x, for the main loop's step_right ($2A31) and step_left ($29E7). Not while down (state 4).

Screen copy, characters: copy 22 rows of 40 characters from the char map ($8200 + row * 40, row = camera row $1C + $3D0D) to the playfield (from text row 3, $4478 or $5078 by $38B3): into the back buffer, or into the displayed one when $44 asks for an immediate redraw (then $3D16 = 1). Unrolled two rows per pass, 20 bytes from each end per loop, with the addresses patched into the code at $26AD-$26C3. $3C82 is set while it runs; $3D0D = 1 afterwards so the next copy prepares the row below.
Patched operand: char map address for the first row of the pair (LDA at $26AC); copy_map_chars writes all twelve operands at $26AD-$26C3.
Patched operand (high byte): char map address of the first row.
Patched operand: screen address of the first row (STA at $26AF).
Patched operand (high byte): screen address of the first row.
Patched operand: char map address of the second row (LDA at $26B2).
Patched operand (high byte): char map address of the second row.
Patched operand: screen address of the second row (STA at $26B5).
Patched operand (high byte): screen address of the second row.
Patched operand: char map address of the first row for the X-indexed half (LDA at $26B8).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed read of the first row.
Patched operand: screen address of the first row for the X-indexed half (STA at $26BB).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed write of the first row.
Patched operand: char map address of the second row, X-indexed half (LDA at $26BE).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed read of the second row.
Patched operand: screen address of the second row, X-indexed half (STA at $26C1).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed write of the second row.

Screen copy, colours: copy 22 rows of the attribute map ($5A00 + camera row * 40) into colour RAM from row 3 ($D878; colour RAM keeps only the low nibble, the colour), with the same unrolled loop and patched operands ($27E0-$27F6) as copy_map_chars, then flip the displayed screen buffer $3D0C (unless $3D3C) and allow the next character copy ($3D16). Colour RAM is not double-buffered, so this runs only when the camera has moved to a new row.
Patched operand: attribute map address of the first row (LDA at $27DF); copy_map_colours writes $27E0-$27F6.
Patched operand (high byte): attribute map address of the first row.
Patched operand: colour RAM address of the first row (STA at $27E2), starting at $D878.
Patched operand (high byte): colour RAM address of the first row.
Patched operand: attribute map address of the second row (LDA at $27E5).
Patched operand (high byte): attribute map address of the second row.
Patched operand: colour RAM address of the second row (STA at $27E8).
Patched operand (high byte): colour RAM address of the second row.
Patched operand: attribute map address of the first row, X-indexed half (LDA at $27EB).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed attribute read of the first row.
Patched operand: colour RAM address of the first row, X-indexed half (STA at $27EE).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed colour write of the first row.
Patched operand: attribute map address of the second row, X-indexed half (LDA at $27F1).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed attribute read of the second row.
Patched operand: colour RAM address of the second row, X-indexed half (STA at $27F4).
Patched operand (high byte) for the X-indexed colour write of the second row.
Move player X one pixel down the course (16-bit y in $1E/$20,x) and clear its ramp latch $3C3F,x.
Unused: store y - ground ($3C97) + height ($3C9B) for player X in $22/$24,x. Nothing calls it and nothing reads $22-$25.

After moving: camera_follow ($28D4), then the camera's map row $1C = camera y / 8 and the fine scroll $1A = 7 - (y AND 7). A new row requests the colour copy ($3D15); a character copy is requested ($3D14) while the fine scroll is below 4 and the previous copy has been shown ($3D16).

Point the camera ($26/$27) half way between the two skaters (from the one further up). The one further down is drawn in front ($3CF6). When the gap reaches $3C (60, so 120 pixels), the one behind is taken out of the race for a moment: state 8, penalty flag $3D52/$3D53 (add_penalty), animation cleared, height back to ground. The camera stops at $0750 (camera_at_bottom $29AC). The screen rows of the skaters are $63/$64 = y - camera + $74.

While the camera rests at the bottom: count $3D83 to 10 and flip $3D84; alternately set colour RAM $DA9D to 6 or 3 and $DAED to 2 or 7, making two characters flash: the police car's light (text rows 16 and 18, column 29: $DA9D - $D800 = 16 * 40 + 29).

If move_player flagged a step left ($3CFB,x): move player X one column left ($61,x - 1) unless at column 0 or blocked by the terrain of the left-hand cell ($3CAB,x: types 1-4 and 7 always, 5 unless the centre is also 5, $0E while the ground is under $18); a blocked step bounces it (wall_bounce $2A7D). Counts down the bounce timer $6D,x.
The right-hand counterpart of step_left: flag $3CFD,x, column $61,x + 1 up to $98, blocked by the right-hand cell's type $3CA9,x.
Bounce player X off a side obstacle, at most once per 5 steps ($6D,x): sound $0A and the heading negated.

From the band-0 interrupt. A player in state 8 (left behind) has its board sprite colour cycled ($3D3D/$3D3E). When a new pose is ready ($3D3B) copy both players' sprite X, Y and pointers from $3D29-$3D3A into the shadows $3CB8/$3CC0/$3CD8 at their sprite numbers, merge the X high bits ($3D11) and write the eight colours $3CD0 to $D027. Players whose slot is still empty ($3D4B < 2) are hidden. Then all eight sprites: X/Y to $D000-$D00F, pointers to both screens ($53F8, $47F8), enable $3CE1, priority $3CE2, multicolour $3CE3, X high bits $3CE0.
Sprites 0 and 1 are the players' shadows: hidden (Y 0) unless the player's shadow mode $3CB4,x is 1 (shadow_mode1 $2CE0) or 2 (shadow_mode2 $2D19).

The sparkle over a smashed object, on sprite $3D7A, while neither shadow is in use: each 4 frames ($3D7C) step $3D7B down; the frame's sprite pointer is $3C22,y and its Y adjustment $3C2F,y; it is placed over map row $3D7D / column $3D7E relative to the camera (Y = (row - $1C) * 8 + $37 + adjustment + fine scroll; X = column * 8 + $18 with the high bit), multicolour, colour 1. At frame 4 or 0 it ends ($2CCF).

Shadow for the yard (behaviour_clothesline): sprite X of player X, colour $0C, X-expanded, not Y-expanded, single colour; Y from the map row $3B or $43 (depending on y below or above $90) relative to the camera.
Shadow for type 13 terrain: X- and Y-expanded, behind the background, single colour; Y from the skater's y ((y - $50)/8 + $95, kept within $9F-$A5) relative to the camera.

From y $0543 on (row 168), while the ground baseline $42,x is above 0 and the terrain is not type $0E or 6: lower the baseline by 2 and move the skater 2 pixels down each frame, so the course's floor steps down by 24 pixels in 12 frames.

Read player 0's joystick from $DC00 + $3D50 and player 1's from $DC00 + $3D51 into $3D4E/$3D4F (active low: bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire). When player 1 is LESTER and a button has been pressed, its byte comes from lester_ai ($32BA, $3D78) instead (only on player 1's call).

Read the joysticks, then run player X's handler for its state and input. While the contact lock $6C counts down, the input reads as nothing pressed (index $1E, the no-fire, no-direction entry). A player with speed 2+ in rough terrain ($3C70) has its directions ignored. The index is the joystick's low nibble times 2 (active low, so $1E is no direction), plus $16 when fire is pressed, plus $36 for a GOOFY player ($3D94,x): the GOOFY half of handler_row_ptrs ($364D) swaps left with right and mirrors the diagonals, and the up and down handlers ($2EFE, $3061) test $3D94 themselves, so GOOFY is the joystick turned half round, but only without fire: the fire entries are the regular ones. Fire adds $16, not $20, so the fire entries 11-15 share their slots with the no-fire nibbles 11-15: the fire slots there belong to nibbles 0-4, all of which hold up and down or left and right together, impossible on a joystick. Every impossible combination selects the null row $3821, whose handlers for states 0-7 are an RTS ($22A1) but whose last two words run on into print_row_lo ($3831): with up and down, or left and right, held in state 8 the handler is $2800 (the middle of copy_map_colours) and in state 9 it is $7850, inside the attribute map. The player on port 1 ($DC01) shares its lines with keyboard row 7, which check_keys leaves selected ($DC00 = $7F), so that player can also steer with the keys 1 (up), left arrow (down), CTRL (left), 2 (right) and SPACE (fire), and 1 with left arrow, or CTRL with 2, produce such a combination; in the simulator, holding up and down on port 1 at PRESS YOUR BUTTON sent the program into the map data until it hit a BRK. The row (27 per half) holds ten handler addresses, one per state $3C59,x (0-9; 10 or more as 0); the chosen one is patched into the JMP at $2E2E.
Low byte of the handler JMP at $2E2E, patched by dispatch_controls from the chosen handler row.
High byte of the handler JMP at $2E2E.
State 0 with no direction (and with fire alone): when the spin $3C5F,x is 0, ease the lean back to 0 (lean_return $2E3B).
Move the lean $3C5B,x one step towards 0: positive through lean_left ($2E51), negative through lean_right ($2E91). The lean only takes the values -1, 0 and +1.
Move the spin $3C5F,x one step towards 0 each call: positive through spin_down ($2E6E), negative through spin_up ($2EAE). Called on the ground by the lean handlers and by turn_one_step.

Joystick left on the ground (state 0): first spin_decay, then count the lean's sub-step $3C5D,x down; every 4 frames the lean $3C5B,x goes down one, stopping at -1 ($FF). The lean is what turn_one_step ($1D41) adds to the heading.

Clear the lean and take one from the spin $3C5F,x (the sub-counter $3C61,x wraps at once, so one per call); when the spin reaches -32 ($E0) complete a half turn instead (turn_around $2ED2). Used to bring a positive spin back to 0 on the ground and, with fire and right in the air states, to spin the skater round.
Joystick right on the ground: spin_decay, then every 4 frames ($3C5D,x counting up) the lean $3C5B,x goes up one, stopping at +1.

Count down the jump's spin budget $75,x, clear the lean and add one to the spin $3C5F,x; at +32 ($20) complete a half turn (turn_around). Used to bring a negative spin back to 0, by the air handler while $75,x is non-zero, and with fire and left in the jump and landing states.

A half turn completed: clear the spin and its sub-counter, flip the facing $3C78,x, count the turn ($3C8C,x) and move the heading $3C63,x half a turn ($20) towards the other side (+$20 if negative, -$20 if not).
State 0, joystick down (up for GOOFY, whose rows are the same here): settle the lean (ride_no_input), then accelerate ($2F09), or brake ($306C) for a GOOFY player.
Push off: count $3D1D,x up and every 8 frames add one to the speed $3D1B,x, up to 8.

State 0, fire with up (down for GOOFY): begin a jump. State 2 (the crouch and spring), lean, spin and jump phase $3D01,x cleared, the jump flag $3C72,x set, the facing saved in $3C49,x, the turn count cleared and the spin budget $75,x = $21.

State 2 handler for most inputs: step the jump phase $3D01,x; the pose comes from jump_pose tables by phase/2 (duck $35D2, offset $35DB, offsets $35E4 for $47 and $49), and on even phases the height rises by $35ED[phase/2]. At phase/2 = 9 the skater leaves the ground: vertical speed $FD (upwards), state 1 (air).

State 1 (in the air), every input: jump phase $3D01,x = $10 so the landing crouch starts from the top; without the jump flag $3C72,x (a fall off a ramp or kerb) the pose is cleared ($3017); after a jump the tucked pose ($3CFF = 1, $45 = 0, $47 = $49 = $FF) and, while the spin budget $75,x lasts, spin_up each frame. apply_gravity ($1E8E) moves the height and sets state 3 on landing.

State 3, the landing crouch: clear the jump flag, take the pose from the jump tables by phase/2 and on even phases lower the height by $35ED[phase/2], counting the phase down from $10 (spinning while $75,x lasts). When the phase passes below 0: state 0, spin budget and spin cleared, height = ground $3C97,x, vertical speed 1, landing_check ($3023), pose cleared.
Clear player X's pose adjustments: duck $3CFF,x and the offsets $45/$47/$49,x.

After landing: $3C7A,x = 1 if |spin| is 4 to $1C, else 0 ($3C7A is written and never read). With |spin| $1D or more the half turn is completed (turn_around). The facing is then compared with the one saved at take-off ($3C49) and the speed with 2, but both branches go to the next instruction, so nothing follows from it. A turn count $3C8C,x of 2 or more is cleared.
State 0, joystick up (down for GOOFY): settle the lean, then brake ($306C), or accelerate ($2F09) for a GOOFY player.
Slow down one notch: count $3D1D,x down and when it goes negative take one from the speed $3D1B,x (if not 0) and reset the count to 8. Also called for turns, bumps and rough ground.

State 2 with fire and down (or fire and one of the up diagonals): early in the crouch (phase/2 below 4) the jump is abandoned for a duck (state 0, duck_handler $3092); later the jump carries on (jump_rise).

State 0, fire with down (up for GOOFY): duck. Sets the duck flag $3C6B,x and the duck pose $3CFF,x for this frame (dispatch_controls clears both every frame, so the skater ducks only while the stick is held). A ducking skater is missed by the high attacks and passes under the clotheslines.
State 0, up and right (regular): brake and lean right.
Duck and lean right. No handler row points here: unused.
State 0, up and left: brake and lean left.
Duck and lean left. No handler row points here: unused.
State 0, down and right: accelerate and lean right.
State 0, down and left: accelerate and lean left.
Air handler plus spin_up. No handler row points here: unused.
State 2 with fire and left: jump_rise plus spin_up, starting the spin in the crouch.
State 3 with fire and left: landing_handler plus spin_up.
Air handler plus spin_down. No handler row points here: unused.
State 2 with fire and right: jump_rise plus spin_down.
State 3 with fire and right: landing_handler plus spin_down.
State 0, fire with left: queue attack 2 (facing left, $3C78 = 0) or $0B (facing right) in $3CE6,x, then start_attack.
State 0, fire with right: attack 8 facing left or 5 facing right.
State 0, fire with up and left: attack 3 or $0C, a high attack (a ducking opponent is missed); $0C never lands at all, its hitting frame being $63 (anim_hit_frame $3947).
State 0, fire with up and right: attack 9 or 6, high.
State 0, fire with down and left: attack 1 or $0A, low (an opponent in the air is missed).
State 0, fire with down and right: attack 7 or 4, low.
Lose one step of speed (if any) and go to state 7, then the state 7 handler at once.

State 7, every input. While an animation runs ($3CE4,x) nothing. Otherwise clear spin, lean and duck; if the heading $3C63,x points straight down the hill (0) or straight up it ($20 or $E0, one direction: a full turn is $40 steps, and turn_one_step wraps $20 to $E0) the queued attack $3CE6,x starts as the animation (animate_sequence returns the player to state 0 when it ends); otherwise the heading turns one step a frame towards the nearer of the two first (down from $01-$10 and $F0-$FF, up from $11-$1F and $E1-$EF).

State 8, set by camera_follow ($28FC for player 0, $295B for player 1, with $3D52 for the penalty, add_penalty $2476) when a player has fallen $3C pixel pairs, 120 pixels, behind the other: heading 0, the skater's y moves 3 pixels down the course each frame and it is put back in a lane (reset_after_fall $0F60). Once the other player's y minus its own is under 16 (low bytes only, unsigned) it is reset again, put in state 0 and given the other player's speed.

State 9 (before the race) without fire. With both buttons in ($3D4B = 2) wait_buttons_released ($3248). Otherwise print the name of the next player to press (slot $3D4B: pointer $35FA/$35FC, row $3600, column $35FE, colour $3602) and under it PRESS YOUR BUTTON ($3597) in the blink colour $3604[$3D4B], the blink phase $3D4D flipping every 32 counts of $3D4C. For LESTER as player 1 with one button in, press for it ($325B). Then the standing height and start animation $13.
Both players have pressed: wait until neither port shows fire ($DC00 AND $DC01, bit 4), then put both players in state 5, the control choice.

State 9 with fire: unless both have pressed (or this is player 0 after one press), blank the name and PRESS YOUR BUTTON lines of slot $3D4B with spaces ($35C0) and count the press. The first press decides the ports: $3D50 = X, $3D51 = X EOR 1, so whoever presses first becomes player 0 (the left status block). Then the standing height and animation $13.

LESTER's joystick, for player 1 in practice. Starts from no input ($3D78 = $FF) and acts only in state 0. Finds the last waypoint of lester_waypoints ($3BED: row, column, heading, 11 entries) whose row is not below LESTER's (y/8 + 12) and steers to its column and heading: the heading is mirrored by $20 when facing right; if LESTER is left of the waypoint column it leans right while heading left, leans left if the heading is steeper than four times the distance, and otherwise matches the waypoint heading (exactly: lean and spin cleared); the mirror image when right of it. On the column, heading straight down: if facing away from player 0, fire and up (a jump, $EE); if facing it, attack_or_ride ($33BD). Finally speed: below player 0 on the screen it holds down (accelerate) up to speed 8; level or ahead it brakes down to speed 2.
JMP $338F that nothing branches to: unreachable.
LESTER: clear bit 2 of $3D78 (left), then the speed control.
LESTER: clear lean and spin, then the speed control.
LESTER's speed: if its screen row $63,x is above player 0's, press down (bit 1) while its speed is under 8; otherwise press up (bit 0, brake) while its speed is over 2, and down while under 2.

LESTER facing player 0 on its line: when player 0 is neither down (4) nor finished (6) and within 16 pixels across ($61/$62) and down ($63/$64), fire and right ($E7: attack 8 or 5 by facing); otherwise ride straight.

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($34B5), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($E03E) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($E075) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $3459-$34C4 by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $E705-$E71E after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($E66A), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($E6CA) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $E721 and, when a slot ends, at $E66D.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($E0DF). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $345C) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $345E holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $E3F6.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $E412/$E425 from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $E425).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $3461/$3463/$3465 for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $3462/$3464/$3466 for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $3467/$3469/$346B for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $3468/$346A/$346C for slot offsets 0/2/4.
Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $34C5); the three slots' base pointers are words at $346D, $346F, $3471, read as $346D,x at $E351 and $E671.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($34), read as $346E,x with the low byte at $346D,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $D5, so slot 2 nests at $34D5.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($34).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $E5, so slot 4 nests at $34E5.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($34).

Four note durations per slot, $3473-$3476 (slot 0), $3477-$347A (slot 2), $347B-$347E (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($348B,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $347F-$3482, $3483-$3486, $3487-$348A, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($348C,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $348B/$348D/$348F (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script; a value N set in one tick makes the slot read again N+1 ticks later (checked against SID writes in the simulator). Set by op 8, notes and note commands.

Per-slot gate timer at $348C/$348E/$3490: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and, G+1 ticks after a value G was set, clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($E0A6), starting the release. The shadow $3498,x keeps the gate bit.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $3491/$3493/$3495; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($E04C) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $3492/$3494/$3496: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $3497/$3499/$349B: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.
Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $3498/$349A/$349C; the gate timer clears bit 0 from it, notes set bit 0.
Per-slot loop counter at $349D/$349F/$34A1: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $349E/$34A0/$34A2. Set from sound_priorities ($E778) on start, cleared at end; compared at $E705-$E71E to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $E70A/$E711 when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $E707 when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $34A3/$34A5/$34A7; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $34A4/$34A6/$34A8; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $34A9/$34AB/$34AD (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $34AA/$34AC/$34AE, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $E37E/$E384.

Per-slot octave shift at $34AF/$34B1/$34B3: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $E62C). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($E03E) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $34C5 (slot 0), $34D5 (slot 2), $34E5 (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried; 8 levels per slot. Ends at $34F4.

jam_load_files' table, three columns of 8 indexed by the load number $32: file numbers $29-$30 here, load address low bytes at $3543 (all 0) and high bytes at $354B ($82, $5A, $48, $AA, $40, $E0, $57, $AA): course characters $8200, course attributes $5A00, playfield characters $4800, pose shapes $AA00 (moved to $BA1A), font $4000, sound $E000, sprites $5700, music $AA00.
Load address low bytes for files $29-$30, all 0 (read at $214F into X).
Load address high bytes for files $29-$30 (read at $2152 into Y): $82, $5A, $48, $AA, $40, $E0, $57, $AA.
Busy-wait counts for irq_band2_colours ($23AC), indexed by the fine scroll $3C57 (0-7): $0D for 0-4, $05 for 5-7, so the colour change lands on the same raster position whatever the scroll.

Raster band handler addresses, words indexed by band*2 ($22B9/$22BF): band 0 irq_band0_frame $22DF, 1 irq_band1_playfield $233D, 2 irq_band2_colours $23A9, 3 irq_band3_screen_copy $23D3. raster_irq patches the chosen one into its JSR at $22D3.
High byte of band 0's handler address (band_handlers + 1), read as $355C,x at $22BF.
Raster line of each band's interrupt: band 0 $F6, 1 $45, 2 $4D, 3 $64 (read at $22CC).
The band after each band: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0 (read at $22C7).

Text in ASCII capitals, zero-terminated, printed by print_string ($2244): "DAVID BUNCH  " and, at $3579, "STEVE LANDRUM", two of the game's programmers. Nothing in memory points at either string: credits never shown.
"STEVE LANDRUM" + 0, an unreferenced credit (Stephen Landrum, the lead programmer); followed at $3587 by "BUTTON" + 0, which nothing references either.
"BUTTON" + 0: not referenced (PRESS YOUR BUTTON at $3597 has its own copy of the word).
"CONTROL:" + 0, printed by show_control_choice ($146E) before REGULAR or GOOFY.
"PRESS YOUR BUTTON" + 0, printed under the next player's name by wait_button_handler ($3207) in the blink colour.
"GOOFY  " + 0 (padded to REGULAR's length), the control choice name for $3D94,x = 1.
"REGULAR" + 0, the control choice name for $3D94,x = 0.
"SCORE:" + 0, printed by print_score_line ($09EC).

Seventeen spaces + 0, printed over a status line to blank it (state5_fire_handler $14CE, press_button_handler $326A/$327F); score_counter prints its last six from $35CB ($0ABE) to clear the points popup.

Jump pose tables, nine entries each indexed by the jump phase / 2, read by jump_rise ($2F4D) and landing_handler ($2FBE): $35D2 the duck flag for $3CFF (1 for 0-4 and 8), $35DB the offset $45, $35E4 the offsets $47 and $49, $35ED the height added (rise) or taken (landing) on even phases: 4 at 6 and 7, 1 at 8.
Jump pose: value for $45,x by phase/2 (1 at 3, else 0), read at $2F53/$2FC4.
Jump pose: value for $47,x and $49,x by phase/2 (2 at 6, else 0), read at $2F58/$2F5D and $2FC9/$2FCE.
Height step by phase/2 (0 for 0-5, 4 at 6 and 7, 1 at 8), added to the height on even phases by jump_rise ($2F69) and taken off by landing_handler ($2FDE).
Low bytes of the control choice names by $3D94,x: REGULAR $35B1, GOOFY $35A9 (show_control_choice $148D); the high bytes ($35) at $35F8.
High bytes of the control choice names ($35, $35), read at $1492.

Run-time copy of each player's name pointer, low bytes ($35FA player 0, $35FB player 1), filled by copy_player_names ($2101/$210D) from $FE00/$FE09; high bytes at $35FC/$35FD. The file's bytes are overwritten at every start.
Player 1's name pointer low byte (from $FE09, written at $210D).
Name pointer high bytes, player 0 at $35FC (from $FE01, $2107) and player 1 at $35FD (from $FE0A, $2113).
Player 1's name pointer high byte (from $FE0A).
Status block column per slot: 0 (left) and $14 (20, right half of the top lines), read by every status print.
Status block text row per slot: 1 and 1 (the name line; the control or score line is the row below).
Name colour per slot: 7 yellow (player 0) and $0D light green (player 1), read by print_player_name and wait_button_handler.
The two blink colours of PRESS YOUR BUTTON, white 1 and light blue $0E, indexed by the blink phase (wait_button_handler $321E).
The two blink colours of the points popup, yellow 7 and red 2, indexed by the blink phase $3D4D (score_counter $0A8D).

Sixteen bytes copied by jam_init ($20B2) to zero page $4B-$5A: the single-bit masks 1, 2, 4 ... $80, then their complements $FE ... $7F at $3610, used to set and clear one sprite's bit in the sprite registers' shadows.

Sideways share of the speed by |heading| $3C65 (0-$20, a full turn being $40 steps): 0-15 for 0-$0F (16ths of the speed, rising with the angle), $0A at $10 (square across), then $F1-$FF (-15 to -1) for $11-$1F, pointing back up the hill, and 0 at $20. split_speed ($1E12) keeps the sign in $3C67 and multiplies by the magnitude; the rest of the speed goes down the hill, so a skater never travels uphill.
Twenty bytes after sideways_share (02 02 03 03 04 05 06 07 and twelve 02) that no instruction addresses and simulated play never read; |heading| cannot exceed $20. Purpose unknown.

Pointers to the joystick handler rows, 54 words read by dispatch_controls ($2E0E): index = joystick nibble * 2, + $16 with fire, + $36 for GOOFY. Entries for impossible combinations (up with down, left with right) point at the null row $3821. The GOOFY half turns the stick half round for the rows without fire (left with right, the diagonals mirrored both ways; up and down use the same rows, whose handlers test $3D94 themselves); its fire entries are the regular ones, so jumps and attacks keep their directions.
High bytes of handler_row_ptrs (read as $364E,y at $2E13).

GOOFY half of handler_row_ptrs (index + $36 when $3D94,x = 1), 27 words to $36B8. Without fire each diagonal and side gets the mirrored row: down+right (nibble 5) gets up+left's row $3759, down+left (9) up+right's $3745, right (7) left's $3709, up+right (6) down+left's $3731, up+left (A) down+right's $371D, left (B) right's $36F5; down, up and no input keep $36CD, $36E1, $36B9. The fire entries from $3699 are the same words as the regular half's.

Nineteen rows of ten handler addresses, one per player state 0-9 ($3C59): 0 riding, 1 in the air, 2 jump crouch, 3 landing, 4 down, 5 control choice, 6 finished, 7 attacking, 8 left behind, 9 waiting for the button. This first row is the no-input row: lean_return, air, jump_rise, landing, fall, state5_no_input_handler, state6_handler, attack_handler, left_behind_handler, wait_button_handler. dispatch_controls patches the chosen handler into its JMP at $2E2E.
Handler row for down (both halves): state 0 push_down_handler, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.
Handler row for up (both halves): state 0 push_up_handler, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.
Handler row for right, and left for GOOFY: state 0 lean_right, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.
Handler row for left, and right for GOOFY: state 0 lean_left, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for down and right, and up and left for GOOFY: state 0 accelerate_lean_right, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for up and right, and down and left for GOOFY: state 0 brake_lean_right, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for down and left, and up and right for GOOFY: state 0 accelerate_lean_left, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for up and left, and down and right for GOOFY: state 0 brake_lean_left, state 5 state5_direction_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire alone: state 0 ride_no_input, state 5 state5_fire_handler; state 6 state6_fire_handler, state 9 press_button_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with up: state 0 start_jump, state 5 state5_fire_handler (as every fire row); the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with down: state 0 duck_handler; state 2 jump_cancel_check, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with left: state 0 attack_left; state 2 rise_spin_up, state 3 land_spin_up, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with right: state 0 attack_right; state 2 rise_spin_down, state 3 land_spin_down, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with up and left: state 0 attack_up_left; state 2 jump_cancel_check, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.
Handler row for fire with down and left: state 0 attack_down_left, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with up and right: state 0 attack_up_right; state 2 jump_cancel_check, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

Handler row for fire with down and right (the last row before the null row): state 0 attack_down_right, state 5 state5_fire_handler; the other states as in the no-input row except where named. Fire rows are the same in the GOOFY half.

The row for impossible joystick combinations: eight times $22A1 (an RTS) for states 0-7, but the row is only 16 bytes long before print_row_lo, so its entries for state 8 and 9 are the first four bytes of that table: $2800 and $7850, neither of them a handler (see dispatch_controls).
Low bytes of the 25 text rows' offsets (row * 40), read by print_char ($2216/$2225); the high bytes follow at $384A. Its first four bytes double as the null row's state-8 and state-9 handlers.
High bytes of the text row offsets (0, 0 ... 3), 25 entries; print_char adds $50 for the screen at $5000 and $D8 for colour RAM.
Screen codes of the hexadecimal digits 0-9, A-F; print_bcd ($2279/$2292) uses only 0-9.

Terrain behaviour handlers by terrain type 0-15 (the attribute map's high nibble), patched into the JSR at $1951 by terrain_behaviour: 0 none $1D2A, 1 wall $1A03, 2 crash object $19B0, 3 $19D1, 4 crash object $19B0, 5 none, 6 roll over $1C87, 7 $19F6, 8 hazard $1CDD, 9 ramp $1B67, 10 kerb $1A77, 11 clothesline $1BC7, 12 moving object $1A8D, 13 $1C44, 14 none, 15 rough $1AAE.
Sixteen handlers for the type of the cell to the right of the skater, patched into the JSR at $1966: all sixteen are $1969, an RTS, so the right-hand cell has no behaviour of its own.
Playfield start of each screen buffer, two words: $4478 and $5078 (text row 3), read by copy_map_chars ($2663/$266D) by the buffer it fills.

Sprite shape buffers, two players by three parts: low and high bytes of each part's first block, indexed by player, plus the buffer phase offset at $38C3 (0 or $40): body $5400/$5580 ($38B7/$38B9), legs $5480/$5600 ($38BB/$38BD), board $5500/$5680 ($38BF/$38C1). build_sprite_shapes ($1253 ...) patches them into unpack_shape.
High bytes of the body buffers: $54 (player 0), $55 (player 1).
Low bytes of the legs buffers: $80, $00 ($5480, $5600).
High bytes of the legs buffers: $54, $56.
Low bytes of the board buffers: $00, $80 ($5500, $5680).
High bytes of the board buffers: $55, $56.
Offset of the second buffer of each pair: 0 and $40, indexed by the double-buffer phase $3CB2.
Sprite colours per player: body 7 yellow (player 0) and $0D light green (player 1), written to the colour shadow by set_sprite_order ($1039).
Board sprite colour per player, copied from the event manager's attribute bytes $FE02/$FE0B by copy_player_names ($20F5/$20FB) at every start; written to the colour shadow at $1045.
Player 1's board colour (from $FE0B, $20FB): $0D for LESTER.
Legs sprite colour per player: 2 red (player 0), $0A light red (player 1) ($103F).
Each skater's reach across the screen by heading/4 (0-8: 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 2), then four zeros; read by collision_check ($24D9/$24DD).
Reach down the screen by heading/4 (6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), then four zeros; read by collision_check ($24E2/$24E6) and as the head-on score base by bump_head_on ($0E56/$0E5E).
First sprite block of each player's parts, the buffer phase added: board $54/$5A ($38E5), legs $52/$58 ($38E7), body $50/$56 ($38E9), read by build_sprite_shapes ($1329-$1340).
Legs sprite blocks: $52 (player 0), $58 (player 1).
Body sprite blocks: $50 (player 0), $56 (player 1).

Animation tables, 23 entries indexed by animation number (1-$16; 0 unused), read by animate_sequence on its first call: $38EB first frame (0, 5, $0A ... $BA), $3902 length, $3919 X offset, $3930 frame delay, $3947 hitting frame. Animations 1-$0C are the twelve attacks, $0D-$12 the falls, $13/$14 the start, $15/$16 the wall falls.
Animation lengths in frames: 5 for the twelve attacks, then $14, $0E, $12, $14, $0A, $0A (falls), 2 and 8 (the start), $18 and $0C (wall falls); read at $13BD.
X offset per animation (4 for attacks 1 and 4, else 0), read at $13B0.

Frame delay per animation: 7 for attacks 1-6, $0B for 7-$0C, 5 for most falls and 7 for $13/$14. Entry $16 ($3946) is rewritten by behaviour_wall ($1A3B) with 11 - (speed - sideways speed) before each wall bounce.
Frame delay of animation $16 (the wall bounce fall), 5 in the file, patched by behaviour_wall ($1A3B) so a faster skater tumbles faster.

Hitting frame per animation, compared with the frames left $3CE8 (animate_sequence $13FC): 3 for attacks 1-$0B, so each hits on its third frame of five; $63, never reached, for attack $0C and for the falls and start animations. Attack $0C (fire with up and left while facing right, attack_up_left $310C) therefore never lands on the other skater: a bug or a deliberate dud. Animation $16's entry would be $395D, the first byte of the next table.
Body pose frame for each animation step (198 entries, indexed by anim_first_frame + step), read by animate_sequence ($1421); the legs and board frames of the same step are at $3A23 and $3AE9.
Legs pose frame for each animation step, 198 entries ($1427).
Board pose frame for each animation step, 198 entries ($142D).
resolve_double_attack's row offset for player 1's attack (1-$0C): 0, 6, $0C for the low attacks, 0, 6, $0C, $12, $18, $1E for the others (read at $0CD2).
resolve_double_attack's column for player 0's attack (1-$0C): 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 5 ($0CD6); added to attack_row to index hit_outcome.
Outcome of two attacks landing at once, 36 entries indexed by attack_row + attack_column: 0 both shoved, 1 player 0 falls, 2 player 1 falls, 3 both fall ($0CDA).

LESTER's route, 11 waypoints of three bytes, row, column and heading: (0, $14, 4), ($1F, $15, 4), ($29, $0E, 6), ($3A, $0A, $0A), ($3F, $0E, $0C), ($44, $11, 4), ($66, $18, 8), ($86, 6, $0A), ($93, $19, $0C), ($BC, $0E, 8), ($CC, $14, 4). lester_ai ($32E4) searches it backwards for the last one at or above LESTER's row.
Waypoint columns (lester_waypoints + 1), read as $3BEE,y by lester_ai ($330F, $331A, $336D).
Waypoint headings (lester_waypoints + 2), read as $3BEF,y ($3328, $337D).

Ten (row, column) pairs: where reset_after_fall ($0FAC) puts a skater back on the course, by the last pair whose row is at or above the skater's row (y/8 + 12): (0, $15), ($2B, $0F), ($3A, $0A), ($40, $0F), ($4E, $13), ($69, $17), ($8D, 6), ($94, $1A), ($C0, $0E), ($CC, $13). The column is multiplied by 4 into the skater's X.
Lane columns (lane_table + 1), read as $3C0F,y at $0FB6.
Sprite blocks of the score sparkle by frame $3D7B, counted down (update_score_sparkle $2C52): entries 3-1 $5E, $5F, $60 (small), 12-5 $61-$64 twice (large); $FF at 0 and 4 ends it.
Y adjustment of the sparkle sprite per frame ($2C58): 0, $0F, 0, $10 for the small one's frames 3-1 (from entry 1), $0C, 8, 4, 0, 4, 8, $0C for the large one, so it rises and falls.
Variables. $3C3C-$3C3E: the VIC registers $D018, $D021 and $DD00 saved by save_vic_state ($21D1) at start-up; nothing reads them back. $3C3C holds $D018.
$D021 (background colour) as found at start-up, saved at $21E0 and never read.
$DD00 (CIA 2 port A, the VIC bank) as found at start-up, saved at $21DA and never read; $3C3F-$3C40 follow, the ramp latches.
Per player: set by behaviour_ramp ($1B7B) after it raises or lowers the ground on an odd y, cleared by inc_player_y ($287A) at the next pixel down, so a ramp acts once per two pixels.
Per player: the points popup timer, $B0 when score_counter shows a popup ($0A71), counted down by player_update ($16F6); at 0 the popup is blanked.

File $30, the Downhill Jam's music, loaded at $AA00 by jam_load_files. First the phrase table: 16 phrases, 4 bytes each, two word pointers: the note stream of voice A (sound $15) and of voice B (sound 2). pick_phrase_a ($AAAA) and pick_phrase_b ($AAC3) copy the chosen phrase's pointer into the operand of each voice's 'set note stream' command ($AA8D, $AA9F).
phrase_streams +1: high byte of each phrase's voice A pointer, read as $AA01,x by pick_phrase_a ($AAB9).
phrase_streams +2: low byte of each phrase's voice B pointer, read as $AA02,x by pick_phrase_b ($AACC).
phrase_streams +3: high byte of each phrase's voice B pointer ($AAD2). The table runs to $AA3F: phrase n's four bytes are at $AA00 + 4n.

Sound script subroutine: voice A's instrument, set again before every phrase. Control $40 (pulse wave, gate off), pulse width $0400, attack/decay $4A, sustain/release $E7, octave shift 1, note durations 5, $0B, 2, 0 (6, 12, 3 and 1 ticks) and gate lengths 2, 8, 0, 0; then into music_play_loop.
Voice B's instrument: pulse wave, width $017F, attack/decay $15, sustain/release $B6, octave shift 3 (lower), durations 5, $0B, $FF, 0 and gate lengths 3, 9, 0, 0; then into music_play_loop.

The voices' shared loop: op $07 plays the next note-stream event, $00 ends the tick, and the jump repeats it. A $FF in the note stream ends the loop: the driver treats it as a return and goes back to the caller of the set-up subroutine (sound_op7_note_stream, $E4B6).

Sound $15, the music, requested by deliver_pending_sound ($091C) after start-up or when the Commodore key turns it back on. Pokes 0 into phrase_toggle, current_phrase and previous_phrase, copies $AB3E into $AB3F (random seed), queues sound 2 (voice B), then voice A: note stream phrase_00_a, and for ever: its instrument (music_voice_a_setup), the phrase, pick_phrase_a ($AAAA) through op $0A, and the next phrase's stream. Priority 9.

Voice A's per-phrase loop: op $87 sets the note stream to the word at $AA8D (patched by pick_phrase_a), gosub music_voice_a_setup plays the phrase, op $0A calls pick_phrase_a, and the jump comes back here.
Operand of voice A's 'set note stream' command, the current phrase's voice A stream; written by pick_phrase_a ($AAB6) from phrase_streams.
High byte of voice A's note stream operand, written at $AABC.

Sound 2, the music's second voice, queued by sound $15 (op $02 at $AA83), never by the game code: note stream phrase_00_b, then for ever its instrument (music_voice_b_setup), the phrase, pick_phrase_b ($AAC3) and the next phrase's stream. Priority 9.
Voice B's per-phrase loop: set the note stream from the word at $AA9F (patched by pick_phrase_b), play it with music_voice_b_setup, call pick_phrase_b, repeat.
Operand of voice B's 'set note stream' command, written by pick_phrase_b ($AACF).
High byte of voice B's note stream operand, written at $AAD5.

6502 code called by voice A's script (op $0A, $AA92) at the end of each phrase: choose_next_phrase, then copy voice A's stream pointer of phrase current_phrase from phrase_streams into the operand at $AA8D. Returns A = the phrase.

Called by voice B's script ($AAA4) at the end of each phrase: choose_next_phrase, then copy voice B's stream pointer of current_phrase into the operand at $AA9F. Both voices end a phrase in the same tick (every phrase's two streams have the same length), so this picks up the phrase voice A's call chose.

Flip phrase_toggle; on every second call (the first voice to finish a phrase) choose the next phrase: from the 9-byte row of phrase_successors for current_phrase take entry 1 + random below the count (random_below $AB2A), and try again while it equals previous_phrase, so the music never goes straight back to the phrase it came from (A, B, A).
