Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). Called only by deliver_pending_sound ($0930), which passes on the one request of the frame, and by sound op 2. Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $E659 with interrupts disabled. No caller in the Jam (opcode scan); part of the shared driver.
Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.
Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in the Jam.
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in the Jam.

One sound tick, called from the band-1 interrupt ($239B) once per frame counted in $3D89: start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $E0C3).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $E0F7/$E107 (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($E652), 1 set register ($E117), 2 queue sound ($E1DB), 3 poke/wait ($E1EA), 4 add ($E255), 5 jump/loop/call ($E2E4), 6 compare ($E38A), 7 note stream ($E443), 8 wait ($E63A), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($E69A), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $E0F7); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $E384.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $E37E this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.
Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $E40C, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $E40B it gives 0, 'less'.
Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $E536 by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration, 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width. $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $E4A0 and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.
Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length; starts the gate timer (flag bit 5) but does not set the gate bit itself.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length; starts the gate timer without setting the gate bit.
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($34AF,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($3473); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($347F); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08 N: set the slot's wait timer, so the script resumes N+1 ticks later (once a $00 has ended this tick). $88 G: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released G+1 ticks later while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.

Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. The Jam's music calls pick_phrase_a ($AAAA) and pick_phrase_b ($AAC3) in file $30 this way, and sound $11 calls $EBDD and $EBF2, two small routines that change the bounds its frequency sweep compares against.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $E6AB when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $E778) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_lo/hi ($E74A/$E761), clear its timers and stack, set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.
